title: Adaptive hysteresis fallback smoothing for FlashAttention v3 under mixed streaming workloads
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Problem: We observe oscillatory kernel handoffs and transient latency spikes when FlashAttention v3 (FA3) kernels are selected on mixed streaming traffic with a broad distribution of sequence lengths and frequent small-batch single-request decodes. Root cause hypothesis: rapid, flip-flopping decisions by the kernel selector combined with v3 startup costs cause short-lived regressions that cascade into SLO violations. Goal: introduce an adaptive hysteresis mechanism that smooths kernel fallback/activation decisions (both v2 <-> v3 and quantized variants) and provide telemetry gating to detect regressions early during rollout.
background: Recent rollouts of FA3 on dedicated pools showed 95th pct latency regressions on tails for sequences < 64 tokens during bursty decode workloads. Current selector uses instantaneous scoring and a short cooldown; this is insufficient when per-request startup overhead and cross-request caching effects dominate. We need a hysteresis multiplier tied to observed end-to-end decode latency, KV cache hit rates, and quantized kernel success telemetry.
design_decisions: Introduce two-layer hysteresis: a short-term exponential-weighted decision window (seconds) and a medium-term occupancy-aware hold (minutes).
Score dampening: multiply v3 advantage scores by a dynamic dampening factor derived from recent tail-latency delta vs baseline.
Graceful activation: when switching to v3, enable a soft-warmup mode that pre-allocates workspace and runs a fast synthetic prefill probe on a fraction of requests.
Telemetry gating: require both improvement in median tokens/sec and no tail-latency spike above threshold before global rollout expansion.
Fallback smoothing for quantized paths: add per-model quant success ratio threshold to avoid bouncing when quant kernel fails intermittently for certain shapes.
acceptance_criteria: No >5% increase in 95th pct latency on mixed streaming benchmark (seq <= 512) vs current canary baseline.
Reduction in kernel selection flip-rate by >= 60% during synthetic burst tests.
Rollout gating telemetry emits alarm when new hysteresis logic misbehaves (latency delta, error rate, quant failure rate).
Unit/integration tests for hysteresis math and deterministic decision replay added to runtime test harness.
experiment_plan: Build local runtime variant with hysteresis knobs behind feature flag (ff:attn_hysteresis_v1).
Run synthetic microbenchmarks: single-request decodes (1-4 batch) and small bursts (100 QPS for 30s) across shapes [8..512].
Measure metrics: kernel flip-rate, 50/95/99 latency, tokens/sec, kv-cache-hit-rate, quant-failure-ratio.
Canary on dedicated pool subset (5% capacity) with traffic shadowing for 24h, monitor SLOs and costs.
If stable, staged increase to 25% then 100% with telemetry gates.
rollback_criteria: quant_kernel_failure_rate > 0.5% for a model over 5 minutes
kernel_flip_rate increases vs baseline or flips exceed 3 flips/minute for >10 minutes
errors linked to out-of-memory or workspace allocation spikes
implementation_notes: Hysteresis state stored ephemeral in runtime node memory keyed by model+shape+quantized flag.
Expose knobs: short_window_ms, medium_hold_seconds, dampening_floor, probe_fraction.
Add deterministic replay endpoint to feed real traffic samples and verify selector decisions offline.
Coordinate with packing/batching team to ensure hysteresis respects batching incentives (don't punish batch throughput).
testing_notes: Add unit tests covering edgecases: shape churn, intermittent quant failures, cold-start sequences.
Integration test harness to run 10k replayed real requests with ground-truth baseline to validate decision parity.
Memory/heap safety fuzzing for hysteresis table to avoid leak under high-cardinality models.
